//: The Mosaic SDUI vocabulary — the single source of truth for what a client renders and what the emit-side may author. It has three tiers and they are generated, never hand-written: `primitives` are the native vocabulary every client must implement (growing this set needs a client release — ADR 0024); `components` are definitions, authored as data in definitions/*.json and delivered by the Platform at runtime (free); `actions` are the behaviours a client interprets. Run `go run ./tools/genui` to regenerate the authoring builders and the vocabulary registry; do not hand-edit the generated files. `go run ./tools/genui -lint` fails when any tier drifts from another — that check is the whole reason this file is one file.
//typeSeparator: The separator between a module's id and its own type name. Core types — every primitive and every component in this file — are unprefixed and may not contain it; a module's types are `moduleId:type`. One character, chosen because it cannot appear in a module id and reads as a namespace in every client language.
//bindingMarker: The single key that makes a prop value a binding rather than a literal. An object is a binding only when it has exactly one key and that key is this one — the same closed-set discipline the action-kind check uses, so a prop that happens to carry a field of this name is never silently reinterpreted. It is spelled the same as a definition template's binding because it means the same thing: resolve a path against a scope. Making it one concept rather than two that share a spelling is the point.
//version: The vocabulary version a client declares on Attach. The server emits only what the declared version supports. Additive growth is a minor bump; removing or changing the meaning of a primitive, prop or action is a major one and needs a deprecation window.
//surfaces: Where an overlay is presented. A closed set for the same reason the validator set is closed: a surface the server names and the client cannot present fails open, showing nothing.

actions.doc: Navigate pushes a screen, optionally with params.
Invoke runs a server mutation, optionally with input.
Play starts playback of a part.
OpenURL opens an external URL (the client validates the scheme).
Back returns to the previous screen.
Query re-reads a screen's data without changing the route.
OpenOverlay presents a node as a modal, sheet or drawer.
Sequence runs several actions in order, stopping at the first failure.
SetValue writes a value into a named field in the enclosing form scope.
Submit runs an action with the enclosing State scope's values merged into its input. `field` names where they merge — a path into the input, or empty for its top level.

validators.name: pattern
validators.doc: RE2 regular expression the value must match. RE2 rather than PCRE so every client can compile it and none can be made to backtrack.

validators.name: matches
validators.doc: Another field's name whose value this must equal — the confirm-password case.

validators.name: oneOf
validators.doc: The value must be one of these.

predicates.name: equals
predicates.doc: {field, equals} — the named field's value equals this.

predicates.name: notEmpty
predicates.doc: {field, notEmpty: true} — the named field has a value.

predicates.name: oneOf
predicates.doc: {field, oneOf: [...]} — the named field is one of these.

primitives.doc: Box is the layout container every composition is built from.
primitives.native: The irreducible layout leaf. A definition is a tree of primitives, so the base case cannot itself be a definition. It also resolves style.responsive against the live viewport, and visibleWhen against the live State scope — two render-time branches no static tree can carry.

props.doc: Layout and surface style, including the responsive override.

Structured predicate over the enclosing State scope's values; absent means always visible. On a field it hides one control, and on a Box it hides a whole branch — which is what makes a multi-step form expressible at all. Without it a wizard is either one long page or a round trip per step, and a round trip per step means every step's answers travel back down in the next tree.

primitives.doc: Text renders a run of text in a token style. Children render after the text, for inline nesting.
primitives.native: The irreducible text leaf.

Variant, weight and colour token.

primitives.doc: Image renders a remote or proxied image with a placeholder fallback.
primitives.native: Loading a resource, handling decode failure and falling back to a placeholder are client behaviours. It also feeds the art-light sampler, which reads decoded pixels.

primitives.native: Resolves a name to a vector the client ships. The glyph set is a client asset, not data.

primitives.native: A transparent grouping node the expander needs in order to return several nodes where one is expected.

primitives.doc: Outlet marks the point in a definition's template where the caller's slot content is substituted.
primitives.native: It is the definition expander's own mechanism. A definition defined in terms of Outlet cannot itself be expanded without it, so it must be native.

props.doc: Slot name filled from the caller's slots map.

primitives.doc: NavItem is one entry in the app frame's navigation.
primitives.native: Owns active-route state: it compares the current screen against its own target, which only the client knows.

Leading icon.

primitives.doc: NavBar groups NavItems into the frame's responsive navigation.
primitives.native: Presents as an inline bar or a bottom tab strip depending on the viewport — a render-time branch, not data.

primitives.doc: Tabs shows one panel at a time behind a tab strip. Each tab's content goes in the named slot matching its id, not in the ordered child list — an ordered child is dropped.
primitives.native: Owns the active tab index.

props.doc: Tab descriptors, each an id and a label.

primitives.doc: Rotator cross-fades through its children on a timer.
primitives.native: Owns a timer and derives the active index from it, and republishes the active slide's palette to the acrylic surfaces.

props.doc: Dwell time per slide in milliseconds.

primitives.doc: State declares named variables and scopes them to its subtree. Children bind to them by name, and a setValue action writes them.
primitives.native: It holds values across renders. A tree is a description of one moment; something has to remember what was typed between two of them, and no arrangement of static nodes can. It is also the scope boundary itself — which of two enclosing States a name resolves to is a question only the renderer, walking its own tree, can answer.

props.doc: The variables this scope declares: each a name, a type (string, number or boolean) and an initial value. Declared rather than inferred so a client knows a name exists before anything writes to it, and knows what to coerce a written value to.

primitives.doc: TextInput is a bare text entry field.
primitives.native: Owns its input value between keystroke and submission.

primitives.doc: Player is the playback surface.
primitives.native: The client owns the decoding pipeline and the transport controls (ADR 0047, ADR 0070). A scrub bar cannot be driven over a network at frame rate.

props.doc: Playback URL issued by the Platform.
Title shown in the player chrome.
Poster shown before the first frame.
Container MIME type.
Seconds to seek to once the media is seekable.
Content node this playback reports progress against.
Release actually being played.

Authored subtitle scripts the client draws itself — each a src, a format, a language, a label and whether it is the one the viewer's preference chose (ADR 0115). They ride beside the HLS subtitle renditions rather than replacing them, so a client that cannot render a script ignores this and still has subtitles.

sugar.doc: OnTap sets the node's primary action.

FacetCount sets how many items a narrowing would leave, shown inside the chip that offers it. A string rather than a number because it is a label: the count is formatted where the fact is known, and a chip is not the place to decide how a large number reads.
Title sets a screen or component title.
Subtitle sets a card/row subtitle.
Poster sets a poster image URL.
Backdrop sets a hero backdrop image URL.
Logo sets a hero clearlogo/title-treatment image URL.
Overview sets a synopsis/overview string.

Message sets the explanation beneath an empty or error state's title. Banner takes its message positionally; every other component that carries one needs this, and without it the emit-side sets the key by string — which is how a prop nothing renders gets shipped.
Progress sets a 0..1 watched fraction.
BadgeText sets a corner badge on a card.
ActionLabel sets a Section's "see all" action label (paired with OnTap).
Meta sets a hero's meta line (year, type, rating).
Genres sets a DetailHeader's genre list.
ResumeAt sets the position in seconds a Player starts from (ADR 0046).
MimeType sets the media type a Player should expect, so a client can pick a pipeline before it fetches.
NodeID names the item a Player is playing, so the client can report its position back against it (ADR 0046).
PartID names the release a Player is playing, recorded with the position so a resume returns to the same encode (ADR 0046).

SubtitleTracks are the authored subtitle scripts a Player may draw itself (ADR 0115). Deliberately not named Subtitles: Subtitle is a different prop on a different tier, and two builders one letter apart is how a prop ends up set on something that does not render it.
Disabled greys a control and stops it emitting.
IconName names the glyph a control or row shows. It is not called Icon because Icon is the primitive that renders a glyph as a node of its own; this sets the `icon` prop of something that draws one.
ItemWidth fixes a carousel's track width in px.
Gap sets the space token between a container's children. Stack takes it positionally; a Grid that wants something other than its default says so with this.
MinColumnWidth is a grid's smallest column before it reflows, in px.
Rating sets a displayed score.
RatingLabel is the source a rating came from.
Year sets a release year.

Index is an episode's place in its series as the design writes it — "S2 E7". A string rather than the episode number, because the season is half the answer and a row that says only "7" is ambiguous the moment a season control sits above it.
Runtime is a human-readable duration.
Thumbnail sets a row's still image.
Watched marks an episode as already seen.

Credits sets a hero's crew line — "Created by X · Directed by Y". One string rather than a list, because it is one sentence with the source's own separators in it; a list would make the joiner a client decision and the client has no way to know whether "and" or "·" is right.
Quality is a release's resolution and dynamic range as one phrase — "4K HDR", "1080p". Display-only: it names what a viewer would recognise, not what a decision engine ranks on.
Lines are a fact card's body, one short statement per line. Separate from Meta because Meta's entries are pills on one row and these are stacked sentences.

Compact is the search screen's heading treatment: a small uppercase label rather than a title, and the heading itself becomes the way into the thing it names. One flag because it is one treatment — a results group is labelled, counted and entered from the same line.

PinAction keeps a Section's onward link visible instead of revealing it on hover. A rail whose heading is the only way into a catalog cannot hide that link behind a pointer, which no remote control has.
Kicker is the eyebrow line above a hero's title.
NativeTitle is the original-language title shown beside the localised one.
ProgressLabel describes progress in words ("24m left").
ShowTags reveals a hero's tag row.

OverlayTitle lays a tile's title over its artwork instead of beneath it, for a card that is mostly image — the hero's up-next dock. Off by default, because a title on the picture is only legible when the tile is large enough to carry a scrim under it.
Avatar sets a person's portrait.
Role is a person's part — a character, or a crew credit.
Align sets a stack's cross-axis alignment.
Justify sets a stack's main-axis distribution.
Wrap lets a stack run onto more than one line.
Retry is what an error state's try-again control emits.
Share is how much of a whole a bar represents, as a percentage the server computed. The server sizes it because only it knows what the whole is.
Depth is a row's level in a tree, as a space token to indent by. Distinct from Indent, which is a bool saying a nav row is nested under the one above it: one is how far, the other is whether.
Buckets are a histogram's bars — each a label, a count and the height the server sized it to.

StatusTone is the colour a row's status marker takes, named as a colour token because the server decides what a level or a status means and the client only draws it. Named StatusTone rather than Tone because the TypeScript binding already exports a `Tone` *type* — the tones enum — and a helper of the same name shadows it.
Rows are an info panel's label/value pairs.
Sources are the resolved streams a picker offers.
Options are a select's choices.
Capabilities are the provider roles a module declares, as chips.
Summary is a card's one-line description.
Value is a field's current value.
Placeholder is a field's empty-state hint.
Help is the note under a field.
InputType selects the keyboard/validation a field asks for.

Validators are the rules a client enforces before it submits — the six the contract declares, no more. A server rejection lands in the same slot (ADR 0089), so this is the fast half of one statement rather than the whole of it. It is sugar because a field's rules were being set with ui.Prop("validators", …) at every call site in every module, which is precisely the untyped setting that let ui.Subtitle onto a Stack.

VisibleWhen hides a node until a predicate over the enclosing State scope holds. Absent means visible; unreadable means hidden, because a control shown because its rule could not be read is the fail-open case.

FieldLabel names a field's control. Named FieldLabel rather than Label because every other component that carries a label takes it positionally — ui.Button(label, …) — and a second, optional way to set the same key on those would be two spellings of one prop.

Chrome selects which frame the app shell draws: "media" — the floating pills over a full-bleed hero — or "admin", the solid bar the settings side of the app wears. Named rather than a boolean because the two are different rooms in the same building, and a third (a player, a setup wizard) is a case rather than a second flag.
Breadcrumb is the trail after the brand in the admin chrome — "/ Settings". It says where you are on a side of the app that has no hero to say it for you.
Lead is the sentence under a panel's heading saying what the panel is for. Distinct from Summary, which explains one row.
Heading titles a frame's panel.
Selected says a section was asked for rather than defaulted to — what lets one payload drill down on a phone and show two panes on a desktop.
Indent nests a nav row under the one above it — an installed extension beneath the store it came from. One list that reads as a hierarchy rather than two lists.
Active marks the open nav row.
HasPrev enables a pagination's previous control.
HasNext enables a pagination's next control.
PrevAction is what a pagination's previous control emits.
NextAction is what a pagination's next control emits.

On is a switch's state. Distinct from Value, which is a field's text: one prop key cannot be a string in one component and a boolean in another, and a switch that read \"true\" as text would render on for the string \"false\" too.

Origin is where a thing came from — an extension's id, version and repository. Distinct from Meta, which is a hero's variadic meta line: the same key cannot be a string in one component and a list in another.

Vars declares a State scope's variables — each a name, a type ("string", "number" or "boolean") and an initial value. Declared rather than inferred: a client must know a name exists before anything writes to it, and must know what to coerce a written value to.
Name is a field's name in the enclosing State scope.
SubmitAction is what a Form emits when it is submitted, with the scope's values merged into its input.
SubmitLabel is the text on a form's submit control.
Busy marks a form as awaiting its submission's result.
Error is a form-level failure message, distinct from a field's own.
OnAppear is emitted the first time this node becomes visible on screen. The server decides what that means by choosing the action; a client never reports anything it was not asked to.
OnDisappear is emitted when this node leaves the screen, having been visible.

A11yLabel is the accessible name, for when the visible content is not one — an icon-only control, an image that carries meaning. It is deliberately not `label`: a visible label and an accessible name are different things, and one key meaning both is how a control ends up announced as its own caption.

HeadingLevel is 1-6, the depth of a heading in the screen's outline. Stated rather than inferred from text size, because size is a design decision and outline depth is a structural one — and a screen reader navigates the second.
Live marks a region whose changes should be announced: "polite" waits for a pause, "assertive" interrupts. Anything else is not announced.

Focusable marks a node that can take focus. Stated rather than inferred from interactivity: a card that navigates is focusable, and so is a heading a TV viewer needs to land on to read, and only the emit-side knows which.
FocusGroup makes this node's focusable descendants one stop in the tab order, moved between with the arrow keys — the roving pattern. A rail of forty cards is one stop, not forty.
InitialFocus asks for focus when this node first appears. At most one per region wins; a screen naming two is stating a preference it does not have.

NextFocus overrides where focus goes from here, per direction — {up,down,left,right} to node ids. It is an override, not the mechanism: a client works out the rest geometrically, and this is for the cases geometry gets wrong.

HasMore says this list is a page of something longer. It is the server's statement, not the client's inference: a page that happens to be full is not evidence there is another one, and a client guessing from the count asks for a page that does not exist.
LoadMore is what fetches the next page. It carries whatever cursor the server needs, because only the server knows what 'next' means for this list — a skip count here, a token elsewhere.

slots.doc: Actions fills the "actions" slot (a hero's CTA row).

slots.name: aside
slots.doc: Aside fills the "aside" slot (a hero's docked poster).

slots.name: action
slots.doc: ActionSlot fills the "action" slot (an empty state's call to action).

slots.name: bleed
slots.doc: Bleed fills a screen's edge-to-edge "bleed" slot (a cinematic hero).

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: Footer fills a frame's "footer" slot (level controls, not sections).

slots.name: content
slots.doc: Content fills the app frame's "content" region — where the current screen renders.

slots.name: topbar
slots.doc: TopBar fills the app frame's "topbar" slot.

slots.name: account
slots.doc: Account fills the app frame's "account" slot.

components.doc: Screen is the root of a server-defined page.
Section is a titled band.
Carousel is a horizontal snap-scrolling rail.
Grid is a responsive auto-fill grid.
Stack arranges children; direction is "horizontal" or "vertical".
Hero is a featured banner. Fill its call-to-action row with Actions.
PosterCard renders a work/item card.
Button carries an action; variant is primary/secondary/ghost/danger.
Badge is a small pill; tone is one of the Tone values.
Banner is an inline message; tone is one of the Tone values.
DetailHeader renders a node's metadata (title, meta, genres).
EpisodeRow renders one episode under a season.
PersonChip is a cast/crew chip.
GenreTag is a genre chip.
FilterChip is one selectable narrowing on a browse surface: a pressable pill that draws its own selected state, with an optional count of what it would leave.
EmptyState is a titled empty placeholder, with an optional explanation beneath it and a call to action.
AppShell is the application frame (ADR 0031): the brand bar, the nav and the region the current screen renders into.
DetailHero is a title's cinematic header — backdrop, logo and the actions docked over it.
Divider is a rule, optionally labelled.
ErrorState renders a Platform error category as something a person can act on.
ExtensionCard is one extension module — what it is, what it can do, and where its bytes come from (ADR 0081).
IconButton is a Button reduced to its icon; the label stays for assistive tech.

InfoPanel is a docked facts panel — a rating and a run of label/value rows. The mockups draw a control under it ("Change device"); it is not here because Mosaic has no device registry to change between, and a panel is the wrong place to learn that.

FactCard is one labelled card in a row of technical facts — what a release is, how it will be delivered, where its metadata came from. Distinct from InfoPanel because the shape is different and so is the job: a panel answers about the title in label/value pairs, a card states three short facts about one aspect of it and sits in a grid of siblings.
MediaTile is a landscape card for episodes and continue-watching.
Pagination is a prev/next pair. The server supplies both targets; the client does no arithmetic.
PlaybackBar is the resume strip for something already started.
RelatedRail is a titled rail that says so when it is empty.
Select is a labelled dropdown over server-supplied options.
SettingsFrame is the Platform-owned settings chrome (ADR 0038): a nav beside the panel the open section fills.

SpanRow is one span of a waterfall: its name, indented by depth, a bar showing its share of the whole, and its duration. The share is the point — a waterfall exists to answer which part of this was the time, and a duration alone does not.

DetailPanel is a titled working surface: a header carrying a name, an identifier and a summary, over a body. Flat rather than acrylic — it is the administrative side of the app, where there is no artwork behind the surface for the material to bend.

StatCard is one figure with a name over it — a percentile, an error rate, a throughput. Distinct from FactCard, which states three short sentences about an aspect of something; this states one number and exists to be scanned in a row of its siblings.

LogTable is a run of structured records as a table — time, level, service, message and the trace that produced it, in fixed columns. A table rather than a stack of cards because the columns are how you read a log: the eye runs down one of them looking for the line that is different.

LatencyHistogram is a distribution as bars — where the time actually went, which a set of percentiles summarises and cannot show. Bars carry their own count and label; the server sizes them, because only it knows what the tallest bucket is.
TraceRow is one trace in a list: what ran, its id, how long it took, and a status dot when something inside it failed.

SettingsRow is one line of a settings panel — a label, an optional explanation of what it does, and a control or a value on the right. It is the workhorse of every panel in the design, which is why it is a component rather than a Stack assembled per screen: a panel that builds its own rows is a panel that drifts from the others.
SettingsNavGroup is one labelled run of settings nav rows.
SettingsNavItem is one settings nav row. The server marks the active one — it is the side that knows the params (ADR 0039).
SourcePicker lists the resolved sources for a Part.
StatusIndicator is a coloured dot with a label.
TextField is a labelled text input with optional help.
Toggle is a switch with a label. It carries the value it moves TO — the client reports the flip, the server decides what it means.

Form is a State scope with a submit control: it declares the fields' variables, hosts them, and emits its submit action with their values merged in. Composed rather than native — it is a State, an Outlet and a button, and nothing about it needs client code.
Component is the generic constructor for a type without a helper (a standard component like SeasonSelector, or a module's own).

//roles: The accessible roles a node may declare. Closed, like the validator and predicate sets and for the same reason: a role is a statement the client must *map* — to an ARIA attribute on the web, to a Compose semantics property, to a UIAccessibilityTrait — and one the server can name that a client maps to nothing produces a control that is invisible to a screen reader while looking correct to everyone else. Chosen for what this vocabulary actually contains rather than transcribed from the ARIA specification, which would be a list nobody could implement completely.
//focusDirections: The directions a nextFocus override may name. Four, and closed: a direction a client cannot resolve leaves a remote control pointing at nothing, and 'the focus went nowhere when I pressed right' is the least reportable bug there is. Diagonals are absent deliberately — no remote has them, and inventing them would make every client implement a geometry nobody presses.
